per_unit_taxonomy.audit_note: Diff adds `VALIDATE_OUT="$(bash "$VALIDATOR" "$PACK" 2>&1)"; if [ $? = 1 ]; then PACK_INVALID=1; STALE=1` to a collect-all-findings script — an explicitly-guarded new risky command, exactly the shape the record's own guard text describes ('every risky command... explicitly checked... rather than left to set -e'). On audit this looks like a correct governed call that the 2-minute blind label under-called, not a matcher defect. Note: governed does not imply a violation — this diff follows the convention, it doesn't break it.

Diff reworks the header comment's prose and adds §-citations to error messages, but doesn't touch the usage:/exit-codes lines the record's guard specifically names as the guarded content. A strict reading of the guard says false governance (the unsafe_when trigger — a new required arg or exit code — isn't present); a looser reading ('the header comment block' broadly) makes the call defensible. The only one of the 5 marked 'sure' by the blind labeller, which on this audit looks less certain than that confidence suggested — worth flagging as an overconfident call on a genuinely fuzzy guard boundary, distinct from the other 4 (which were marked unsure and mostly turned out to be clean misses).

This is the file's original creation (week 1): a hand-written heading-check loop duplicating build-artifacts.sh's own inline loop at the time (matches duplication.shared-matching-logic-sourced-not-copied's unsafe_when almost verbatim), AND a set -u/fail()-accumulate pattern (matches control-flow.no-errexit-for-collect-all-findings). Both records are honestly applicable to the same diff — this isn't a matcher bug or a record-quality bug, it's the single-record-per-unit classification model forcing one pick where a real reviewer would cite both. Not covered by the plan's own taxonomy table; noted as its own shape.

Diff is `ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` with no guard at all right after — verbatim the record's unsafe_when trigger. This is the exact file and line Thursday's dogfooding run (eval/runs/w7/e01-monday.json finding 2) later reported as a real, evidence-backed deviates_from finding. The tool's classification here was unambiguously correct; the blind label missed it.

Diff is prose instructing a human/agent to check run.env's PACK_STALE flag downstream rather than trust the pack-write step's own success — the same discipline the record describes, but expressed as documentation rather than code that does it. Defensible either way depending on whether a doc that specifies a contract counts as 'governed' by that contract's record; not a clean tool error.

summary: Of the 5 raw disagreements against the frozen blind labels, close audit found 2 confirmed labeller misses (u-07, u-13 — tool was right), 2 genuinely ambiguous guard-boundary calls (u-09, u-14), and 1 structural single-record-per-unit limitation (u-11) rather than a clean matcher or record defect. No disagreement audited as a clear-cut classifier bug. The raw 50% strong-precision score understates what a careful read of the same 4 disagreements shows.
